title: Right scalar homogeneity of the symplectic form
statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, and equip $V = \bbf_p^n \times \bbf_p^n$ with the symplectic form $\omega(u,v) = \sum_{i=0}^{n-1}(x_i z'_i - z_i x'_i)$, where $u = (x,z)$ and $v = (x',z')$. Then for every scalar $c \in \bbf_p$ and all $x, y \in V$,
\[
\omega(x, c\,y) \;=\; c\,\omega(x, y),
\]
where $c\,y$ denotes componentwise scalar multiplication.
hypotheses_covered: n arbitrary natural number (dimension of each factor)
replaced:
Let $p$ be prime and work over the space $V = \bbf_p^n \times \bbf_p^n$ equipped with
the symplectic form $\omega(u,v) = \sum_{i=0}^{n-1}(x_i z'_i - z_i x'_i)$, where $u =
(x,z)$ and $v = (x',z')$. Then for all $x, y, z \in V$,
\[
\omega(x + y, z) = \omega(x, z) + \omega(y, z).
\]
